references.text: The same ritual with blood on the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe was first performed on Aaron himself before being repeated on his sons in verse 24.
The same pattern of applying blood to the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe is used in the cleansing ritual for lepers.
In the cleansing ritual for lepers, oil is applied to the same places where blood was applied during the priestly consecration.
Blood from the guilt offering is applied to the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe, following the same pattern as in the priestly consecration.
Oil is applied to the same places as the blood, in accordance with the ritual described in the priestly consecration.
The commandment to apply blood to the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe on Aaron and his sons is first given in Exodus.
The blood is sprinkled around on the altar, following the same practice described in verse 24.
The blood is sprinkled around on the altar, consistent with the description of Moses' actions in this verse.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to how Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle and all the vessels used for service, emphasizing that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law.
